sections.title: Letter name and sound
paragraphs: You name this letter (We) /veː/. It has one sound. You hear it in (Wasser) /ˈvasɐ/, which means water. It is a consonant, a sound made when the mouth narrows the air.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch your upper teeth gently with your lower lip. Push the air through the small gap between them. Turn on your voice so your vocal cords vibrate. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzz.

sections.title: When to use it
paragraphs: This letter makes its sound in all native words. You hear it at the start of (Wasser) /ˈvasɐ/. You also hear it after other letters, such as in (zwei) /tsvaɪ̯/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say this letter like the first sound in water. Do not form a circle with both lips. Instead, place your top teeth against your lower lip, like the v in vine.
